title: Volunteering
text: Volunteering give people the chance to help their community and learn new skills at the same time. Last semester, I volunteered at local food bank once a week. We sorted boxes of food and packed bag for families in need. It was very satisfied to see how much our work helped people. I also became friends to other volunteers from many different countries. Since then, I volunteer at two other events. Volunteering can also help students win work experience, which is useful when they apply for jobs after graduation.

errors.ruleReminder: An -ing subject (volunteering) is singular and takes a singular verb.
errors.explanation: The subject is volunteering, one activity, so the verb needs -s: gives.

errors.ruleReminder: A singular countable noun needs an article (a, an, the) or another determiner.
errors.explanation: Food bank is a singular countable noun, so it needs an article: a local food bank.

errors.ruleReminder: A countable noun with no article must be plural when you mean more than one.
errors.explanation: They packed many bags, so the noun must be plural: bags.

errors.ruleReminder: Use -ing adjectives for the thing (satisfying) and -ed adjectives for the feeling (satisfied).
errors.explanation: The experience causes the feeling, so we need satisfying. People feel satisfied.

errors.ruleReminder: Become friends and make friends go with with: friends with someone.
errors.explanation: The phrase is become friends with someone, not to.

errors.ruleReminder: Use the present perfect with since: since then, I have done.
errors.explanation: Since then connects the past to now, so we need the present perfect: have volunteered.

errors.ruleReminder: Some nouns go with certain verbs: gain experience, get experience.
errors.explanation: We gain or get experience. Win is used for prizes and games.
